analysis:
This is a documentation-only change to docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The changed ranges fall in the `darkbloom sandbox` section (head lines ~1256-1527). It adds the `setup --disk <volume>` work-disk option, the Work disk checks, the Plan/Install steps that pass `--disk`, the plan `disks` fields and the `status --json` `disks` member. No source code, keys, auth paths or coordinator contracts change, so the PR itself introduces no security regression.

Relevant threat model: TB-013 and T-061 (tampered installer or add-on run as the Mac's owner) and A-019. The documented download flow (lines 1302-1311) is unchanged in kind. The installer comes over HTTPS only, redirects go only to https, the response is capped at 1 MiB with a `#!` first line check, and it is written 0600 in a 0700 directory. The doc explicitly states that the CLI does not verify the script beyond TLS and that the installer verifies the add-on release. This matches the existing T-061 posture.

The new `--disk` handling needs implementation review in SandboxWorkDisk.swift and SandboxInstaller.swift, which are not supplied. Paths are made absolute and passed to a script run as the owner. The doc describes ownership-enable via `sudo diskutil` run in the foreground with the terminal. The CLI never reads the password, and it never formats a drive. Open questions for the code: argument-injection or quoting of disk paths passed to `/bin/sh`, whether the symlink and `/Volumes` mount validation is robust (TOCTOU), and whether the work-disk path expands the add-on's blast radius. These are unverified implementation contracts, not doc-evidenced regressions.

The prefix-cache threat T-041 covers operator-selected external APFS volumes, but sandbox work disks are a separate add-on feature. No cross-file interaction was found in the supplied evidence. The patch excerpt is truncated, but both head units were read in full.
